parameters.content:
## Match participants from form submissions and schedule 1:1 Google Meet calls with Google Calendar: innovation-networking.de Clone

Sometimes you want to match people only within a specific group, e.g. at the n8n event "IN THE LOOP 2026". This workflow lets you share a form, collect sign-ups, and match people automatically at a deadline.

### Who's it for
Event organizers, community managers, network initiatives and companies who want to connect participants one-on-one, for example within a meetup, conference, cohort or internal innovation program, without matching people by hand.

### How it works
1. Participants sign up via an n8n form with name, email and an optional short description. Sign-ups are stored in an n8n data table with status "registered".
2. Settings (deadline, matching criteria, meeting time, duration, title, time zone) come from an optional Google Sheet; empty or missing values fall back to the "Default Settings" node.
3. After the deadline, the form shows that the event is over and no longer saves sign-ups.
4. Every 15 minutes, the workflow checks whether the deadline has passed and then loads all open sign-ups. Duplicate emails are removed.
5. An OpenAI model forms pairs based on your matching criteria (one group of three only if the number of participants is odd).
6. For each pair, a Google Calendar event with a Google Meet link is created and an invitation email with the date and link is sent via Gmail.
7. Matched participants are marked as "matched" with their partners and meeting link, so they are not matched again.

### How to set up
- [ ] Create a data table (Overview > Data tables > Create), e.g. `matching_participants`, with the String columns `name`, `email`, `description`, `status`, `partner_emails`, `meeting_link`, and select it in "Save Sign-up", "Load Open Sign-ups" and "Mark as Matched".
- [ ] Connect your OpenAI credentials in "OpenAI Model".
- [ ] Connect Google Calendar in "Create Event with Meet" (uses your primary calendar by default).
- [ ] Connect Gmail in "Send Invitation Email".
- [ ] Fill in "Default Settings", **or** create a Google Sheet with row 1 = `matching_deadline`, `matching_criteria`, `meeting_start`, `meeting_duration_minutes`, `meeting_title`, `timezone` and row 2 = values, then connect Google Sheets and select it in "Settings from Google Sheet".
- [ ] Publish the workflow and share the form URL (/form/matching-signup).

### Requirements
- OpenAI account (API key)
- Google account with Google Calendar and Gmail
- Optional: Google Sheets for managing the settings without opening the workflow
- An n8n instance with data tables

### How to customize the workflow
- **Time zone:** all times use the `timezone` setting (default: Europe/Berlin). Use an IANA name such as "America/New_York"; invalid values fall back to the default.
- **Matching:** adjust the rules in `matching_criteria` or the prompt in "AI Matching", e.g. to match by industry, location or complementary skills.
- **Meetings:** change meeting start, duration and title, or edit the invitation text in "Send Invitation Email".
- **New round:** enter a new `matching_deadline` and `meeting_start`, adjust the criteria if needed, and share the form link again.

### Why Code nodes?
- **Settings:** merges Google Sheet values with the defaults field by field and converts different date formats (incl. sheet serial numbers) in your time zone.
- **Prepare Participants:** removes duplicate emails, stops when fewer than 2 people signed up, and builds the participant list for the AI.
- **Build Pairs:** double-checks the AI result so nobody is matched twice or left out; unassigned people are paired automatically.

### About the initiative: 
https://innovation-networking.de is a volunteer initiative to strengthen innovation. We connect innovators with each other: regularly once a month, every 2nd Wednesday, for 30 minutes at 4:30 pm. These conversations bring new perspectives, which is what it is all about. Anyone who likes the initiative can join as a partner.

## Start workflow triggers

Two entry points start the workflow: a public sign-up form submission and a scheduled check that runs every 15 minutes.

## Load event settings

Applies default matching settings, pulls optional overrides from Google Sheets, and merges them so sheet values take priority over defaults.

## Accept open sign-ups

Checks whether sign-up is still open, saves valid form submissions to the Data Table, and shows a confirmation response to the participant.

## Handle closed submissions

Handles form submissions that arrive after the event or sign-up window has closed and returns an appropriate message to the user.

## Load participants for matching

Checks whether the configured matching time has arrived, then loads currently open sign-ups and prepares participant data for the AI matching step.

## Generate participant pairs

Uses an OpenAI LLM chain with a structured JSON parser to create participant pairings, then transforms the AI result into pair records for scheduling.

## Schedule and invite pairs

Creates a Google Calendar event with a Google Meet link for each pair and sends the participants an invitation email.

## Update matched participants

Extracts the members from each scheduled group, splits them into individual participant records, and marks each person as matched in the Data Table.
